claims.claim: Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.
claims.evidence: For every graph, τ(G)=n−α(G), so τ(G)≤k iff G has an independent (n−k)-set. Complementation bijects these graphs with graphs containing K_{n−k}, proving the formula. The endpoint formulas follow directly; for k=1, nonempty star subgraphs are counted once except single-edge graphs, which are counted twice. Exhaustive enumeration of every labelled graph through n=6 confirmed all 28 complement cases and every stated endpoint.
claims.search_method: Direct bijective proof, endpoint inclusion-exclusion, and exhaustive exact-integer enumeration for 0≤n≤6.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).
claims.evidence: For a fixed k-set C, precisely q edges have at least one endpoint in C, hence exactly 2^q graphs have C as a cover. Every graph with τ≤k has a k-cover by extending a smaller cover, and retaining it only for its lexicographically first k-cover counts it exactly once. At most binom(n,k)^2 polynomial-time tests are made per 2^q-scale enumeration, giving 2^{q+O(n)} time and polynomial space. Since q≤kn, this is 2^{o(n²)} when k=o(n). Exact enumeration confirmed the canonical count for all 28 pairs 0≤k≤n≤6.
claims.search_method: Independent enumeration and complexity analysis, supplemented by exhaustive exact-integer canonical-cover checks.

claims.claim: For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.
claims.evidence: For a cover C and X⊆C, replacing X by U_X gives a cover exactly when X is independent in G[C]. Consequently C is minimum iff |U_X|≥|X| for every nonempty independent X. Equality yields another minimum cover, and fixed-cardinality lexicographic comparison makes C earlier exactly when min X<min U_X, equivalently U_X has no label below min X. The stated capped-count/boolean state records precisely these conditions. There are at most 2^t−1 coordinates, at most 2(t+2) values per coordinate, 2^t neighborhood types, and 2^{binom(t,2)} choices for G[C], yielding the displayed fixed-k polynomial bound. The exact DP matched brute-force counts for all 28 pairs through n=6; 13,225 individual exchange and lexicographic characterizations were also checked.
claims.search_method: Independent exchange-argument proof, DP state audit, and exhaustive exact-integer comparison against brute force.

claims.claim: Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.
claims.evidence: Summing the number X of independent m-sets over all graphs gives S1. For an ordered pair of m-sets intersecting in j vertices, exactly 2binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) edges are forced absent, giving the stated S2=sum X². The support of X is F(n,n−m); hence 1_{X>0}≤X gives the upper bound and Cauchy–Schwarz gives F≥ceil(S1²/S2). Fixing one independent m-set gives F≥2^q, while binom(n,m)≤2^n gives the logarithmic bracket. Direct exact moments and every bound were confirmed for all 21 pairs 1≤m≤n≤6.
claims.search_method: Independent double-counting and Cauchy–Schwarz proof, plus exhaustive exact-integer moment evaluation.

claims.claim: At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.
claims.evidence: P_n counts a graph together with an ordered proper two-coloring. If C(x) is the EGF for connected labelled bipartite graphs, then B(x)=exp(C(x)) and P(x)=exp(2C(x))=B(x)^2 because each connected component has exactly two ordered colorings. Coefficient extraction gives the recurrence, whose O(n²) big-integer operations have polynomial bit complexity. Since every bipartite graph is triangle-free, B_n≤T(n,3), and complementing reverses this to F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n. Exact recurrence values matched brute-force bipartite counts through n=6, and the endpoint bound passed for n=3 through 6.
claims.search_method: Independent labelled-EGF coefficient proof and exhaustive exact-integer graph enumeration.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for one exact 2^{o(n²)}-time algorithm for arbitrary input pairs (n,k). The draft proves that exponent only in the restricted regime k=o(n); for typical k=Θ(n), its q is Θ(n²). Its fixed-k result is likewise nonuniform in growing k, while the moment formulas and bipartite recurrence provide bounds rather than the requested exact count. The final writeup explicitly acknowledges these limitations and labels the resolution PARTIAL, so it neither fully resolves nor overclaims the target, but it does establish material correct progress.
checks_performed: Read the exact target from the authorized source input and audited only the authorized iteration-5 draft; did not use the web or any prohibited report, database, receipt, prior run, or other solution.
Independently proved the complement equivalence, endpoint counts, canonical-cover enumeration, fixed-k exchange characterization, moment identities, and bipartite recurrence.
Persisted and ran an exact-integer checker covering every labelled graph through n=6.

Confirmed 28 complement cases, 28 canonical-cover cases, 28 fixed-k DP totals, 13,225 exchange/lexicographic cases, 21 moment cases, the bipartite recurrence through n=6, and four triangle-free endpoint bounds.
Checked target coverage separately from claim correctness and confirmed that the uniform arbitrary-k target remains unresolved.
